common_name: Montgomery Rabbiteye Blueberry (Vigorous Mid-Season Southern Blueberry)

planting.note: Plant in late winter to early spring; in zone 8-9 plant December-February for best establishment. Montgomery is a vigorous, productive rabbiteye blueberry cultivar bred for reliable mid-season production and good fruit quality in Southern growing conditions. Plant with a different rabbiteye cultivar for cross-pollination.

directions: Plant in acidic (pH 4.5-5.5), well-drained sandy or loamy soil with pine bark amendment in full sun. Montgomery is a vigorous rabbiteye blueberry cultivar developed for Southern growing conditions, producing a reliable mid-season crop of medium to large, firm berries with good flavor. The bushes are notably vigorous and productive, establishing quickly and bearing well once mature, making Montgomery a dependable choice for filling out a mid-season harvest window alongside earlier and later rabbiteye selections. Like all rabbiteye blueberries, it requires cross-pollination from a different rabbiteye cultivar to set a full crop, so plant at least two different varieties within 50-100 feet of each other. Mulch heavily with pine bark or pine straw to maintain the acidic, moisture-retentive soil rabbiteye blueberries need, and avoid soils with a pH above 5.5, which causes chlorosis and poor growth. Prune out old, unproductive canes each winter to encourage vigorous new fruiting wood.

common_name: Columbus Rabbiteye Blueberry (Late-Season Large-Fruited Southern Blueberry)

planting.note: Plant in late winter to early spring; in zone 8-9 plant December-February for best establishment. Columbus is a University of Georgia rabbiteye release ripening late in the season with large, good-quality berries, extending the Southern blueberry harvest window. Plant with a different rabbiteye cultivar for cross-pollination.

directions: Plant in acidic (pH 4.5-5.5), well-drained sandy or loamy soil with pine bark amendment in full sun. Columbus is a University of Georgia-released rabbiteye blueberry that ripens late in the Southern blueberry season, extending fresh harvest well past most mid-season cultivars while still producing large, flavorful fruit on vigorous, productive bushes. Pairing Columbus with earlier-ripening cultivars like Austin, Alapaha, or Premier gives a Southern blueberry planting a long, staggered harvest from late spring through midsummer. Like all rabbiteye blueberries, Columbus requires cross-pollination from a different rabbiteye cultivar to set a full crop, so plant at least two different varieties within 50-100 feet of each other. Mulch heavily with pine bark or pine straw to maintain the acidic, moisture-retentive soil rabbiteye blueberries need, and avoid soils with a pH above 5.5, which causes chlorosis and poor growth. Prune out old, unproductive canes each winter to encourage vigorous new fruiting wood.

common_name: Onslow Rabbiteye Blueberry (Vigorous Productive Southern Blueberry)

planting.note: Plant in late winter to early spring; in zone 8-9 plant December-February for best establishment. Onslow is a North Carolina-released rabbiteye blueberry noted for strong vigor and heavy, reliable production. Plant with a different rabbiteye cultivar for cross-pollination.

directions: Plant in acidic (pH 4.5-5.5), well-drained sandy or loamy soil with pine bark amendment in full sun. Onslow is a rabbiteye blueberry cultivar released for the Southeast, valued for exceptional plant vigor and consistently heavy production of medium to large, good-flavored berries. Its strong growth makes it well suited to establishing a productive planting relatively quickly, and it performs reliably across the range of soil conditions typical of Southern blueberry patches, provided the acidic, well-drained requirements common to all rabbiteye types are met. Like all rabbiteye blueberries, Onslow requires cross-pollination from a different rabbiteye cultivar to set a full crop, so plant at least two different varieties within 50-100 feet of each other. Mulch heavily with pine bark or pine straw to maintain the acidic, moisture-retentive soil rabbiteye blueberries need, and avoid soils with a pH above 5.5, which causes chlorosis and poor growth. Prune out old, unproductive canes each winter to encourage vigorous new fruiting wood.
